nature: judgement grounded in artifacts, not a new measurement

sources.v1_holdout: experiments/EVAL-HOLDOUT-001 (reported in handoff; results not opened)

ce_rejected_at_dev.rule: net = rescues - regressions > 0 on strict Recall@10

verified_process_strengths: preregistration written before any scores exist
frozen system config hashes; a changed field changes the hash
corpus snapshot reproduces to an exact manifest hash
contamination-aware split, not random; holdout access-logged
EVAL-VAL-001 rejected SYSTEM-B when it failed to replicate
EXP-015 refused to substitute a hand-rolled reranker rather than fake a result
EXP-018B Track 1 proved score-preservation bitwise, not by tolerance

concerns_ranked.concern: the cross-encoder is probably not paying for itself
concerns_ranked.evidence: +1 case of 20 at 11.5x latency, and MRR falls 0.8309 -> 0.8239
concerns_ranked.missing: D vs D-without-CE on V2-DEVSET-001 (n=50). EXP-016's comparison is n=20.

concerns_ranked.concern: n is too small for the decisions being made on it
concerns_ranked.evidence: EXP-018 is +2 cases on n=50; EXP-016 is +1 on n=20; systems.py itself notes six of the last seven experiments turned on one or two cases
cases mined from the corpus then reviewed; favours extractive lexical retrieval and likely explains the recurring 'answer is visible but does not rank' finding
6454.8 ms retrieval before generation; ~3360 ms after PERF-002 D1; ~550 ms without the CE
202 documents / 14209 chunks; BM25 IDF and routing conclusions may not hold at 100x

recommended_next: run the CE ablation on V2-DEVSET-001 before spending more on CE latency
get real unmined questions, even 30, from actual usage
treat ~6.4 s retrieval-before-generation as not shippable
verdict: The discipline is excellent and the V1 holdout number is real. The risk is not sloppiness - it is that the rigour is being spent on differences too small to be real, and that the most expensive component has the weakest evidence behind it.
